understanding: A ground-investigation tender priced from the client's own bill. The register carries the commercial risk (liquidated damages and payment terms lead), the take-off gives the drilling quantities the engine prices from, and the gates show where it stands: the review is the open one, and the estimate cannot move until its lines are decided [gate:review]. The bill's own state says what remains before a defensible total exists [bill].
disagreements: Where the estimator's hole classification and the bill's Class A / Class B counts disagree, one of them is wrong — the reconciliation strip on Site is the place to look before pricing the rig moves.

proposed_actions.reasoning: Open register lines block the review gate, and everything after it. Deciding them is the highest-leverage human act on this tender right now.

proposed_actions.reasoning: The class counts are the only external check the bill offers on access classification, and unclassed holes keep it open.
Any cost with no bill item and no route is a promise to do that work for nothing (General Preambles ¶6). The sweep is the only hard stop — clear it before the total is read as real.
